questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) She go (B) to school (C) every morning (D) without fail.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'She' needs 'goes', so 'She go' is wrong.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) The childrens (B) are playing (C) in the (D) park.
questions.explanation: 'Children' is already plural; 'childrens' is incorrect.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) He do not (B) like (C) hot (D) tea.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'He' needs 'does not'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) I am (B) elder than (C) my (D) brother.
questions.explanation: 'Elder' is not used with 'than'; the comparison needs 'older than'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) They was (B) very (C) happy (D) yesterday.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'They' needs 'were'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) She can (B) sings (C) very (D) well.
questions.explanation: After the modal 'can', the base verb 'sing' is required.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) There is (B) five books (C) on the (D) shelf.
questions.explanation: The plural 'five books' needs 'There are'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) He is (B) more stronger (C) than (D) John.
questions.explanation: 'Stronger' is already comparative; 'more' is redundant.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) My father (B) go to office (C) by (D) bus.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'My father' needs 'goes'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) The sun (B) rise (C) in the (D) east.
questions.explanation: The singular 'The sun' needs 'rises'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) We (B) enjoyed (C) during (D) the holidays.
questions.explanation: 'Enjoy' needs a reflexive object here: 'enjoyed ourselves'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) Each of (B) the students (C) have (D) a book.
questions.explanation: 'Each of' takes a singular verb 'has'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) One of (B) my friend (C) is (D) a doctor.
questions.explanation: 'One of' must be followed by a plural noun: 'my friends'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) He is (B) junior than (C) me (D) in office.
questions.explanation: 'Junior' is followed by 'to', not 'than'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) The news (B) are (C) very disturbing (D) today.
questions.explanation: 'News' is singular and takes 'is'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) I have (B) been living here (C) since (D) ten years.
questions.explanation: With a duration, use 'for': 'for ten years'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) She said (B) that she (C) will come (D) tomorrow.
questions.explanation: In reported speech after a past reporting verb, 'will' becomes 'would'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) Neither of (B) the two boys (C) were (D) selected.
questions.explanation: 'Neither of' takes a singular verb: 'was'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) He returned back (B) home (C) late at (D) night.
questions.explanation: 'Returned back' is redundant; 'returned' already means came back.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) The teacher (B) gave us (C) many informations (D) in class.
questions.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable: use 'much information'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) He prefers (B) coffee (C) more than (D) tea.
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' is followed by 'to', not 'more than'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error, or choose 'No error': (A) Hardly had he (B) slept (C) when the phone (D) rang.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly had ... when' with the simple past is correct, so there is no error.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) Each student (B) and each teacher (C) were (D) present.
questions.explanation: 'Each ... and each ...' takes a singular verb: 'was'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) The quality (B) of the mangoes (C) were (D) not good.
questions.explanation: The subject 'quality' is singular: use 'was'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) The number of (B) students in the class (C) are (D) increasing.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' is singular: use 'is'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) He is one of (B) the best players (C) who has (D) ever played.
questions.explanation: 'One of the ... who' takes a plural verb agreeing with 'players': 'who have'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) Being a hot day, (B) we decided (C) to stay (D) indoors.
questions.explanation: The participle 'Being a hot day' dangles; it should be 'It being a hot day'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error, or choose 'No error': (A) No sooner did he (B) see the police (C) than he (D) ran away.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner ... than' with the correct structure has no error.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) She is (B) more intelligent (C) than any girl (D) in her class.
questions.explanation: Since she is one of the girls, the comparison needs 'than any other girl'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) I could not (B) help to laugh (C) at (D) his joke.
questions.explanation: 'Cannot help' is followed by a gerund: 'help laughing'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) He insisted (B) to go (C) with (D) us.
questions.explanation: 'Insist' is followed by 'on' + gerund: 'insisted on going'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) Ram is taller (B) than any student (C) in (D) his class.
questions.explanation: Ram is himself a student in the class, so it must be 'than any other student'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) Scarcely had he (B) entered the room (C) than the lights (D) went off.
questions.explanation: 'Scarcely ... when' is correct; 'than' is wrong.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) The teacher, (B) as well as the students, (C) were (D) present.
questions.explanation: 'As well as' does not change the number of the subject 'teacher' (singular): use 'was'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) He spends money (B) like water (C) despite of (D) his poverty.
questions.explanation: The correct form is 'despite' (or 'in spite of'), not 'despite of'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) The list of (B) selected items (C) were (D) very long.
questions.explanation: The subject 'list' is singular, so the verb must be 'was'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) If I would have known (B) about the delay, (C) I would have (D) left earlier.
questions.explanation: The 'if' clause of a third conditional takes the past perfect: 'If I had known'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) The reason (B) he failed (C) is because (D) he did not study.
questions.explanation: 'The reason ... is because' is redundant; use 'is that'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) Hardly had I (B) reached the station (C) when the train (D) had left.
questions.explanation: After 'Hardly had ... when', the second clause takes the simple past 'left', not 'had left'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) One should (B) keep (C) his (D) promises.
questions.explanation: The pronoun must agree with 'one': use 'one's'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) The committee (B) has decided (C) to postpone (D) their meeting.
questions.explanation: The verb 'has' treats 'committee' as singular, so the pronoun must be 'its meeting'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) No less than (B) fifty persons (C) was present (D) at the function.
questions.explanation: 'Fifty persons' is plural, so it needs 'were present'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) He had scarcely (B) gone out (C) than it (D) started raining.
questions.explanation: 'Scarcely ... when' is correct; 'than' is wrong.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) It is you (B) who is (C) responsible (D) for this mess.
questions.explanation: The relative clause verb must agree with 'you': 'who are'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) Neither the manager (B) nor his assistants (C) was available (D) at that time.
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'assistants' (plural): 'were available'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) The scenery (B) of the hills (C) have attracted (D) many tourists.
questions.explanation: 'Scenery' is uncountable and singular: use 'has attracted'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) Each of (B) the participants (C) were given (D) a certificate.
questions.explanation: 'Each of' takes a singular verb: 'was given'.

questions.stem: Choose the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) Not only (B) he insulted me (C) but also (D) threatened my family.
questions.explanation: When a clause begins with 'Not only', the subject and auxiliary are inverted: 'Not only did he insult me'.
